Lena Park: FYI reproducible flake in payments example: when OAuth refresh happens during a streaming generation the client reconnects and we occasionally double-invoice the same logical op. Minimal trace below.

Omar Ruiz: Ack. Which SDK and sampleapp variant?

Lena Park: Node SDK, payments-sample running against hosted-us-west. Trace: 
```
[2026-03-22T09:07:12Z] stream start req=r_11 user=acct_77
[2026-03-22T09:07:13Z] auth refresh for client=cli_3 -> rotated token
[2026-03-22T09:07:13Z] client reconnect attempt=0 (immediate)
[2026-03-22T09:07:13Z] server received duplicate payload fingerprint=fp_01
[2026-03-22T09:07:14Z] invoice created id=inv_202 for fingerprint=fp_01
```

Nina Gomez: That immediate reconnect looks suspicious. If the client retries with no jitter and we don't surface an idempotency key the server treats it as a new request. Do we include any replay guard header for streams today?

Lena Park: Not in Node streaming helper. Python had a last-minute change that attaches an `Idempotency-Key` for all POSTs; Node historically skipped it for streaming.

Ethan Shaw: Two-pronged fix I want to propose: client-side small randomized reconnect delay (e.g., uniform(75,250)ms) + attach a short-lived replay token header e.g. `x-rw-replay-token` (UUID) for stream start. Server can keep a tiny LRU/TTL set and dedupe within, say, 20s.

Omar Ruiz: Agree on replay token, but prefer `x-redwood-replay` to match other headers. Also: for portability, we should keep Idempotency-Key semantics for non-streams and treat replay-token as lightweight hint for the runtime to dedupe.

Nina Gomez: For backoff policy: recommend full jitter with base=200ms, max=25s. i.e. sleep = random(0, base * 2^attempt) capped. We should explicitly call out that reconnects due to auth rotation are "attempts" and must go through the same jitter path.

Lena Park: Good point. Current Node helper bypasses retry path on refresh; it reconnects immediately to avoid additional latency. That's the culprit. Changing that will impact tail latency slightly but reduces dup billing risk.

Ethan Shaw: Server tombstone idea: use Redis with a lightweight key `replay:{replay_token}` -> hash(fingerprint, invoice_id) TTL 25s. On insert we use SETNX; if key exists return a special streaming resume response or 409. Need to watch memory usage for high-traffic routes; consider bloom + occasionally persistent metric.

Omar Ruiz: Also add telemetry: `replay.token_seen`, `replay.duplicate` and a percent of duplicates that resulted in a charge. We should be able to detect client versions that don't send the replay header.

Nina Gomez: Testing plan: update payments-sample to include an e2e that forces token rotation mid-stream and asserts only one invoice. Add a chaos harness to flakily rotate tokens and measure duplicate rate.

Lena Park: I'll add the repro and failing test in sampleapp: tests/stripe_stream_rotation.spec.ts. CI is flaky currently.

ops-bot: sampleapp-e2e #991 failed: stripe_stream_rotation.spec.ts (1 failed) :warning:

Ethan Shaw: Action items: 1) Node SDK: add `x-redwood-replay` header for streaming + small reconnect jitter (owner: @Ethan) 2) Runtime: tombstone prototype + metrics (owner: @Omar) 3) Sampleapp: add e2e + chaos test (owner: @Lena) 4) Docs: short note about streaming idempotency and recommended jitter (owner: @Nina). Can owners ack?

Omar Ruiz: ack 
Ethan Shaw: ack 
Nina Gomez: ack 
Lena Park: ack — I'll link the repro as soon as I push it.

Lena Park: Extra note: prefer configurable defaults so teams with ultra-low tail latency can opt out, but warn strongly.

Omar Ruiz: I'll also prototype an adaptive tombstone eviction: keep a small counter per-route and increase TTL under contention.

Nina Gomez: Nice. Also add a short SDK test that simulates token rotation and asserts the helper delays reconnects by at least the min jitter.

Lena Park: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short RFC linking implementation details and cost estimates.
